key: Minx et al. 2018, 'Negative emissions—Part 1: Research landscape and synthesis', Environmental Research Letters 13:063001 || The State of Carbon Dioxide Removal 3rd Edition (June 2026, Edwards et al., doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/ZRD65), led by the same core author group (Minx, Lamb, Nemet, Smith, Geden), is the direct successor assessment. It reports: current CDR at 2.2 GtCO2/yr (99.9% conventional land-based), in 'maximum ambition' 1.5°C scenarios, CDR accounts for ~16% of cumulative mitigation effort with a central estimate of 8.8 GtCO2/yr in 2050 (range 6.5–13.3 GtCO2/yr), national pledges fall short of 1.5°C-compatible pathways by more than 5 GtCO2/yr by 2050. The State of CDR 2nd Edition (June 2024, doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/F85QJ) had already updated the scenario analysis, reporting 7–9 GtCO2/yr by 2050 in 'more sustainable' 1.5°C scenarios. The IPCC AR6 WGIII (2022) Chapter 12 also provides an updated assessment of CDR methods, costs, and potentials superseding the 2018 figures, and is synthesised in the AR6 SYR [2] which the draft does cite

The 2024 NASEM report 'Accelerating Decarbonization in the United States' references it but does not replace it. The State of CDR series (2023, 2024, 2026) and IPCC AR6 WGIII Chapter 12 (2022) provide more recent international assessments of the same topic
